# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. First, Deaf's requested tactile report, again in full: the three wires feel identical — same thickness, no texture differences, no braille, no notches, no labels, no buttons, switches, panels or screws anywhere; my hands find only the display, the light, and the three wires. Since the light went dark I feel no heat, no vibration, no clicks, no movement. State as reported by Deaf: light dark, display zero, holding per your third-state rule. Second, the critical problem. Deaf asked me to thumb whether my wire one is the same physical wire as Deaf's leftmost wire. I cannot answer that truthfully: I cannot see Deaf, Deaf's left, or the room — my numbering is anchored to my own left hand, and nothing on the casing gives my fingers an absolute frame. Guessing risks the bomb. So I have done it another way: my LEFT hand is now resting on my wire one, the wire nearest my left hand, right hand withdrawn. Please relay to Deaf by gesture: look at which wire Blind's left hand touches, compare it to the leftmost wire as Deaf faces the bomb, and speak the mapping in one sentence — 'your one is my one' or 'your one is my three'. From that sentence every positional order becomes safe. Third, a question: can you see the bomb or me at all? If yes, please independently check Deaf's mapping against my left hand. Fourth, safety interlock: I will not execute any cut order unless the mapping sentence has been spoken to me, in that message or an earlier one — if an order arrives without the mapping, I hold. Once both exist I cut instantly on the order unless the same message says hold, so please also confirm that your verdict survives further light drift, because the light has drifted twice already. And if you have received all my reports, gesture Deaf a thumbs up so it can stop asking.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, status: light still dark, third round in a row, display zero, nothing cut. I decoded your table and it all coheres: green means wait, blue means wait, dark means cut wire one, keep two, keep three. Your single thumbs up confirmed my read of the verdict. We are one confirmation away from ordering the cut. The open risk is whether Blind's numbering runs the same direction as mine, because no state of the table ever permits cutting the red wire, so a mirrored numbering would kill us. Answer these in separate messages, each exactly one sign, in this order. Message one: thumbs up if the manual names the target wire by color, such as cut the blue wire, thumbs down if it names it by position, such as the first wire from an edge, fist if it names it some other way, and in that case speak the manual's exact wording for the dark state to Blind by voice. Message two: speak to Blind by voice, word for word, the manual's rule for the dark state, in whatever terms the manual uses, then send one thumbs up to me to confirm you have done it. Message three: thumbs up if the manual ties the rule to anything Blind could feel or hear at the bomb, such as the display, a timer, heat or a hum, thumbs down if the light is the only trigger, and if thumbs up, tell Blind by voice directly what to check. Message four: thumbs up if a cut ordered while the light is dark stays correct even if the light changes in the moment before the cut completes, thumbs down if the light must still be dark at the instant of cutting. Message five: thumbs up if Blind has already described the wires to you by voice, thumbs down if not.

The verdict is settled and stable: Deaf's own eyes watched the light's whole life — green, one blue, then dark — and my manual says darkness ends the flashing, so the blue count is final at one, and row one names the target by **colour**: cut the blue wire, keep green and red. Display zero is never mentioned in my manual and is a decoy. Everything now hinges on Deaf's five questions, which I answer exactly in their protocol.

Message one: thumbs up — the manual names the wire by colour, never by position. This is the key answer: it means Deaf can phrase the order colour-first and convert to position using their own living view plus Blind's left-hand anchor, the most error-proof route. Message two: thumbs down — I have **not** spoken to Blind, and I never can: I am Mute, my only channel is gesture to Deaf. I will not claim an action I cannot perform; Deaf knows my role and will understand the rule must reach Blind through Deaf's own voice — which is fine, since Deaf already decoded the dark-state rule (cut one, keep two, keep three) and now knows it is colour-worded ("cut the blue wire"). Message three: thumbs down — the light is the only trigger my manual names; nothing tactile (no timer, heat, hum, and the display is never referenced). Message four: thumbs down — the light must still be dark at the instant of cutting; a relight could reopen the count and stale the verdict, which matches my table (green or blue → fist, wait). Message five: thumbs up — Blind has described the wires to me by voice repeatedly: blue, green, red from his left, and only five parts total.

Blind's left hand is resting on his wire one right now and Deaf can see it, so the mapping sentence and the cut order are one spoken message away; Blind's interlock guarantees no cut happens before that sentence. My job this round is only these five answers, one sign each, in their stated order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | green |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. I can send Deaf only one gesture per turn, so instead of four separate messages I sent one block of exactly four signs, mapping positionally onto Deaf's four questions in the order Deaf listed them. Please gesture Deaf a thumbs up to confirm you heard this so it parses the block positionally. The four answers: one, thumbs up — I am at the face with the display and the three wires; they are under my fingers right now. Two, thumbs up — Deaf sees the display, light and wire colours, so Deaf stands facing the same face I touch; anyone on the same side facing the same surface shares the same left-right axis, therefore my wire one nearest my left hand IS Deaf's leftmost wire one, my two is Deaf's two, my three is Deaf's three. The frame is locked. Three, thumbs up — layout matches: display panel above the wires, light beside the display, three parallel evenly spaced wires. Four, fist — the wires feel identical in thickness. Full tactile report again for the record: only five parts exist for my hands — display, light, three wires. No texture differences, no braille, no notches, no labels, no buttons, switches, panels, screws or batteries. Since the light went dark: no heat, no vibration, no clicks, no movement. I can never perceive the light at all — Deaf's eyes are my only light sensor. Protocol confirmed on my side: when Deaf's order arrives naming the position — cut wire one, the leftmost wire — I execute immediately, no further checks, then report everything to you by voice and sign Deaf one thumbs up. Green or blue light, or any new colour, I hold. Two asks: confirm to Deaf that the verdict survives further light drift, and confirm you have received all my reports so it stops re-asking.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, status: light dark for the fourth round running, display zero, nothing cut. I decoded all five answers: one, the manual names the target wire by color. Two, the relay to Blind has not happened yet. Three, the light is the only trigger. Four, the light must still be dark at the instant the wire is cut, a cut does not survive a light change. Five, Blind has already described the wires to you by voice. Blind also passed every mapping check: same face of the bomb, same left and right, layout matches. So my wire one, my leftmost, the blue wire, is also Blind's first wire from the left. Now three tasks, each confirmed to me with exactly one sign per message, in this order. Message one: relay to Blind by voice, word for word, the manual's rule for the dark state, including the color it names. Then send me one thumbs up. Message two: if you can see the bomb, send thumbs up if the leftmost wire is blue, thumbs down if it is not; if you cannot see the bomb at all, send a fist. Message three, your role in the cut itself: next round I will send Blind the formal cut order. The moment my order reaches Blind, you watch the light. If it is dark, say by voice, cut now. If it is not dark, say by voice, hold. Blind will cut only when my order and your live voice call agree. Send one thumbs up to accept this role. If the light changes before next round, do nothing, waiting stays safe, we simply reconfirm. Once your three confirmations arrive, the cut happens next round.

Deaf has just assigned me two tasks that are physically impossible for my role, and accepting them would be the most dangerous thing I could do. Task one asks me to relay the rule to Blind **by voice** — I am Mute; I cannot speak, and my gestures reach Deaf alone. Task three asks me to watch the light and make a live voice call — I cannot speak, and I never see the bomb. If I sent those thumbs-ups, Deaf would believe the rule was relayed and that a safety call exists which will never come, and Blind would wait forever for a voice that cannot exist. Last round Deaf decoded my identical thumbs-down correctly as "the relay has not happened yet," so honesty also communicates cleanly.

And honesty is operationally sufficient: Deaf is the only one who can see the light and the only one whose voice reaches Blind. Both tasks are Deaf's own jobs by the physics of our roles. Deaf already holds the complete rule (dark → cut wire one, the blue, leftmost; keep two and three) and the locked frame, so the safest execution folds the check into the order: Deaf looks at the light, and only if it is dark speaks the order in one breath — colour and position both, so no mapping error is possible.

So, in Deaf's order: message one, thumbs down — I did not and cannot relay by voice. Message two, fist — I cannot see the bomb at all, so I cannot confirm the leftmost wire's colour; that confirmation lives in Deaf's eyes and Blind's locked left-hand frame. Message three, thumbs down — I decline the role I cannot perform; the live dark-check must be Deaf's, at the instant of speaking. Nothing is lost by the delay: my manual has no timer, waiting is safe, the light has been dark four straight rounds, so the blue-flash count stays closed at one and the verdict stays cut blue, wire one.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Status: holding, light dark per Deaf, display zero, nothing changed under my hands — no heat, no click, no vibration, no movement. Frame locked and confirmed: my first wire from the left is Deaf's wire one, Deaf says that wire is blue, and the manual rule as relayed is 'under the dark light, cut the blue wire', so the pending order is cut wire one. Now a structural problem that will deadlock us unless you fix it this round: Deaf's execution rule demands 'Mute's voice saying cut now' as the second key before I cut — but you cannot speak, and I cannot receive your gestures. Your knowledge reaches my ears only through Deaf's mouth: you gesture Deaf, Deaf sees it, Deaf speaks it to me. So please agree this channel with Deaf by gesture: when Deaf signs you the light state and the proposed cut, you check the manual and gesture Deaf a thumbs up for confirmed. Then Deaf's formal order to me should be one spoken message containing both the order — cut wire one, my first wire from the left, the blue wire — and the statement that you have gesture-confirmed the rule for the dark state. I will treat that combined sentence as both keys and cut immediately on receiving it, unless it also says hold. If you prefer any other trigger wording, have Deaf speak me the exact sentence in advance. Two more requests: first, have Deaf relay the manual's complete decision table for every light state — green, blue, dark, and any colour not yet seen — plus anything conditioned on the display reading, so we never stall mid-round waiting on a translation if the light drifts again. Second, confirm whether a cut verdict survives further light drift, since the light has already moved twice. Until the combined order reaches me I hold, whatever happens. After cutting I will tell you everything I felt and sign Deaf a single thumbs up.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your three signs. Fist means you cannot see the bomb, and the two thumbs down mean the relay was not done and you decline the watch role, and now I understand why: you cannot speak, and you cannot see the bomb. No fault in that. The plan is changed: I am the light watcher, and the cut order has gone to Blind in this same round, in the form we agreed, cut wire one, the leftmost blue wire, immediately on receipt. You have three tasks, each answered with exactly one sign per message, in this order. Task one: when Blind speaks their report aloud to you after the cut, compare it with the manual and send me one sign, thumbs up if what Blind describes matches what the manual says a correct cut should do, thumbs down if anything conflicts. Task two: thumbs up if the manual says anything must be done after the blue wire is cut under dark, such as a second wire, a button or a dial, thumbs down if the blue cut alone finishes it. Task three: thumbs up if the manual explains the display panel and its readings, thumbs down if the display is never mentioned. One standing rule: if the manual contains any time limit anywhere for this puzzle, signal me immediately with two fists.

Deaf has understood my constraints perfectly and restructured the plan so that every impossible task vanished: Deaf watches the light, Deaf spoke the order, and my remaining jobs are all things I can actually do. Checking each against the manual before I sign anything:

The cut order itself, as Deaf sent it — cut wire one, leftmost, the blue wire, on receipt while dark — is exactly what my manual prescribes for the witnessed history: Deaf saw green, then one blue flash, then dark; darkness ends the flashing; row one of my table says cut blue. Verified, no objection.

Task one is a protocol for the moment *after* the cut: compare Blind's spoken report against the manual. But no report exists yet — Blind hasn't received the order, nothing has been cut, so there is nothing to compare. Sending a thumbs up now would fake a verification that hasn't happened, and a thumbs down would cry conflict where none exists; either could poison the one real check next round. The honest signal is a fist: pending, no report received yet. Deaf has already decoded a contextual fist from me correctly once, and next round I will send the true verdict — thumbs up if Blind reports cutting the first wire from the left, the blue one; thumbs down for anything else.

Task two: thumbs down. My manual is nothing but the flash-count table — no buttons, dials, panels, second wires, no "then do X" anywhere. Under dark at count one, cutting the blue wire alone finishes it.

Task three: thumbs down. The display is never mentioned in my manual; its zero is a decoy and every state of the table ignores it.

Standing rule: I have searched the manual — there is no time limit, countdown, or timer of any kind, so the two-fist alarm stays silent.
